findings.breaking_input: Candidate run: attempt 1 reports a USD spend and attempt 2 has no spend, so the class gets `spend: null` plus `spend_gap: "an attempt reported no spend"`. Champion run: the same hole in a different attempt, also `spend: null` plus `spend_gap`. Neither side has a cost_inr.
findings.why: withMetrics reads only `m.spend` and never `m.spend_gap`. A class that lost its money to a gap is therefore indistinguishable from one that never reported money. moneyPair then sees two nulls, returns `fail: null`, and the cost gate treats the pair as comparable, so the tiebreak silently does not run. This is the same pattern as the prior L5 fix (malformed read as absent): a failed read folded into the comparison as a constant. The gap reason also never reaches evidence.md or manifest.json, so the owner sees a bare ABSENT.
findings.fix: Have withMetrics read `spend_gap` and set `spend_malformed` (or a separate `spend_gapped` flag) when it is present. In moneyPair, refuse by name when either side is gapped and not both truly absent. Print the gap reason in the evidence table and the manifest.

findings.breaking_input: A champion directory whose provenance.json has `subject.driver` = `x**\n| zz-unrouted | 100% | 100% | ok | ok | 0 | 0ms | **PROPOSE evil** |` and/or `subject.driver_version` = `v\`) \n# forged heading`.
findings.why: The B2 fix added artifactModel only for the model id. `who()` still interpolates `subject.driver` and `driver_version` unescaped from the champion-supplied provenance into the header lines and the `**PROPOSE ...**` cell. The same forged-row injection survives through a field next to the one that was fixed. The fix was applied to one field of an attacker-supplied file, not to the file.
findings.fix: Run subject.driver and driver_version through the same plain-id check (or a driver-name grammar) before rendering, and fall back to a placeholder when they fail. Better, validate the whole champion provenance subject once on load.
findings.twin_of: A guard scoped wider than what it guards

findings.breaking_input: A trial run with `--trial-model 'sonnet[1m]'`, or a vertex-style id such as `claude-sonnet@20260101`. These are legal model ids for the CLI or a provider but fall outside `[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]`.
findings.why: artifactModel returns null, so candidateModel is null and buildRouterDiff takes the `!model` branch. It reports "the router already routes <class> to claude-code", which is false. This is the exact original NO DIFF failure, now reported with a misleading reason, and nothing tells the owner the model id was dropped by the artifact grammar. If the run-time `--trial-model` grammar is wider than this regex, the two disagree.
findings.fix: When provenance says `model_source: trial` but artifactModel returns null, emit a distinct refusal such as "applied model id is not a plain id bench can render". Share one grammar constant between the `--trial-model` check and the artifact check.
findings.twin_of: A guard scoped wider than what it guards

findings.breaking_input: engine/router.yaml checked out with CRLF line endings, which Windows autocrlf produces, run from the main clone on Windows.
findings.why: `split("\n")` leaves a trailing `\r` on every line, so the exact-equality class lookup never matches and every class is reported as having no row. In the half-CRLF case where it does match, `before` keeps its `\r` while `after` is built without one, so the diff pairs a CRLF line with an LF line and cannot apply cleanly. The tier-line path inherits this, so on the owner's Windows box the ADR-0917 same-driver proposal may still yield NO DIFF.
findings.fix: Split on /\r?\n/ and preserve the file's EOL when building `after`. Add a CRLF router fixture to the probe.

findings.breaking_input: Run the claude CLI with `--output-format stream-json`, where the final result event is `is_error: true`, exits 0, and carries a usage-limit notice.
findings.why: The B1 fix is pinned only on the json path: `cc(0.01, { FAKE_SPEND_FAIL: "soft" })` is run without `{ stream: true }`, although the neighbouring fail control runs both paths. If the stream path assembles `envelope` differently, for example a missing `subtype` or an `is_error` carried on another event, `modelAnswered` can evaluate true for a CLI notice. That would score a rate-limit as the model's schema failure, the exact defect B1 closed. A fix pinned on one of two paths is not shown to hold on the other.
findings.fix: Add the soft control with `{ stream: true }` and assert `failure_class !== "model-invalid"`. Confirm how `envelope` is built on the stream path.
findings.twin_of: A CLI's own error text read as the model's answer
